## HueMux v0.0.5-alpha.3 — Sliders that reach the end, and cards that hold still

> **Alpha.** Built and tested in CI, not exercised on real hardware here
> beyond a single LAN deployment. Two changes to how the light list behaves,
> one of them a correction to a rule that was deliberately odd.

### Dragging a brightness to 0 switches the lamp off

Dragging a slider down to 0 used to dim the light to the bridge's floor and
leave it on. A bulb sitting at 1% is doing nothing useful, and switching it off
took a second touch in the same place — a rule that had to be known before it
would work.

The slider now has three outcomes, and they depend only on where the level
started and where it ended:

- **0 → a level** turns the light on at that level. A bare brightness command
  only dims, so a physically-off bulb used to stay dark while the UI claimed
  otherwise.
- **a level → another level** sets the level.
- **a level → 0** turns the light off, in one gesture.

This applies to a single lamp, to a room's slider and to the all-lights slider,
which turns off every dimmable lamp it covers.

### The hover lift on a light card is gone

A card used to rise 2px under the pointer, with a deeper shadow, a brighter
ring and a brighter colour wash. It misfired in both directions:

- On a phone, a tap leaves `:hover` stuck. The card that was touched stayed
  lifted and brighter than every other one until something else was tapped.
- On a desktop, it announced a card as a control, which it is not — a card is
  a container, and the lamp's own buttons inside it carry their own hover
  states, which are unchanged.

The colour wash behind a card is now a fixed part of its identity: it still
dims for a light that is off, and no longer brightens under the pointer.

The Android app carries the frontend inside its bundle, so it needs the APK
from this release.
